ruledBy: Al, bespoke line review rounds 1 and 2
note: Every line here is Al-approved and written for its specific photograph. Keyed by image hash: one hash can occupy two rotation slots and the lines belong to the picture, not the slot. English only - AF is Al's to write, zu/xh/st go to the native-review backlog.
method: Round 1 wrote five per image and Al kept 171 of 196 (87%) once the two transposed briefs were excluded. Round 2 rewrote the 39 gaps under the swap test (PAIRING-TASTE rule 1a) and Al kept 39 of 39. Combined 210 of 235 = 89%. Wind, the weakest bucket in every earlier pass at 48%, ran 80% in round 1 and 100% in round 2.

lines: The Weber has been watching him water that lawn for twenty minutes now.
Coffee in one hand, hose in the other, and the whole day still ahead.
This is the only twenty minutes of the day that belong to him.
The jacaranda is dropping purple on a lawn he has just finished watering.
Nobody inside that house is awake yet and that is entirely the plan.
That number has not moved in eighty kilometres and neither has the scenery.
The aircon is losing and everyone in this car has stopped talking about it.
Saturday, and the only shade for the next hour is inside this car.
Somebody said the padkos would be fine in the boot. Somebody was wrong.
The road ahead has been the same road for a very long time.
That sprinkler has been the best-value thing in this garden all summer.
Those two on the stoep have made their choice and they are sticking with it.
Nobody is going to remember the temperature, only the sprinkler.
Sunday, and the water bill has already quietly accepted its fate.
The lawn is taking a beating that has nothing to do with the sun.
The windpomp has stopped turning, which is how you know the day is over.
That glass has been full for an hour and she is in no hurry.
Sunday, and the Karoo is doing the one thing it does better than anywhere.
The stoep step is still warm and will be for another hour yet.
Nobody has switched a light on inside yet and nobody intends to.
The ice cream is losing and all three of them know it.
Friday, and this promenade is doing the work of six different bars.
Everybody came out at exactly the same time and nobody planned it.
The light will be gone in nine minutes and nobody is hurrying.
That dog has walked this stretch more times than any of them.
The ice in that glass has about four minutes left.
Sunday night, and this promenade is busier than it was all afternoon.
The whole town waited for the sun to go down and then came outside.
That water was cold when somebody put it down there.
Nine at night and the paving is still handing back the afternoon.
Too warm to sleep inside, so the whole family moved under the Milky Way.
Somebody left the light on inside and nobody is going back for it.
The youngest is still awake and has decided the sky is worth it.
Five mattresses on a stoep, and not one of them is a compromise.
Friday night, and the ceiling has been upgraded considerably.
Thursday night, and the balcony has been promoted to the main room.
It is cooler out here at midnight than it was inside at six.
The ice in that jug never stood a chance and everybody knew it.
That curtain is the only moving air in the entire flat.
Nobody is going back in there until the walls let go of the day.
Two in the morning, and that fan has been the loudest thing in the house.
The glass of water was a very good idea about four hours ago.
The net is handling mosquitoes. The fan is handling everything else.
Monday starts in five hours and that fan is not going off.
Somebody has already turned the pillow over twice tonight.
Nobody has been inside that house since about four this afternoon.
The pool has been the only sensible room in the place all day.
Those beers on the edge are on their third owner tonight.
Saturday, and the water is still warmer than the air above it.
The lights went on two hours ago and nobody has suggested moving.
The dog has worked out where the coldest tiles in the house are.
That is the bathroom floor and it is now his bedroom.
Nobody in this house is getting into that bath tonight.
He has been lying there since about eight and has no further plans.
Wednesday, and the dog has made the only sensible decision so far.
The frangipani is dropping flowers all over the paving and taking no responsibility.
Monday night, one lit window, and the rain doing all the talking.
That wall has a damp line on it older than tonight's storm.
The burglar bars are the only straight lines left in the whole street.
Somebody inside has already decided they are not going anywhere tonight.
The gutter is carrying this street's problems straight down to the next one.
Jacaranda blossom and stormwater, which is Joburg's least favourite combination.
The electric fence is fine. The pavement has completely given up.
Wednesday, and the drive home is going to be a story by tomorrow.
Every drain on this road is now working on somebody else's behalf.
The pool is measurably fuller than it was at supper time.
Nobody is going to have to top that up for a month.
The pool light is the only thing in this garden still doing its job.
Tuesday night, and the pool is having a far better time than anyone.
The paving has stopped absorbing anything and is just passing it along.
That umbrella has been closed since the moment it arrived.
Every one of those parking bays was somebody's plan for tonight.
Saturday night at the sea, and the sea has taken the whole promenade.
The painted lines are the only thing out there still holding a shape.
Somebody drove all the way down here to look at this and left.
The tree has seen worse Tuesdays and it will see worse again.
Every gate in this street is shut and every dog has an opinion.
Somewhere behind those walls a whole street is pretending to sleep.
The streetlight is doing overtime that nobody is going to pay for.
Tomorrow morning this road will be covered in somebody else's tree.
The gutter is telling you exactly how long you left it.
The hose reel is going to feel very unnecessary for a while.
Jacaranda season and a Monday, and the paving is taking both badly.
Whoever parked in the street tonight is regretting it right now.
That security light is doing the best work it has done all year.
Friday night, and the stoep has quietly become the whole evening.
That one bulb is holding this entire building together.
The polish on that floor was not designed with this much water in mind.
Everything green out there is having the best night of its life.
You can hear the roof better than you can hear the television.
That car made it under the carport with about four minutes to spare.
The road is still dry, which is the last thing it will be tonight.
A Free State storm gives you exactly as much warning as it feels like.
Everyone on this street is now standing at a window they never use.
The dust and the rain are about to have a very short argument.
The sheets are dry already and the wind is not finished with them.
The Helderberg is clear, the washing is horizontal, and that is Sunday sorted.
That little olive tree is going to grow up with a permanent lean.
Nobody in this house is paying to dry anything today.
Those pegs are all that stands between you and a fence full of sheets.
The bin made it to the pavement and then made its own decisions.
Tuesday is bin day, and the wind has clearly read the schedule too.
Half of this street's recycling is now the hedge's problem.
The oaks are fine. The wheelie bins never stood a chance.
Three houses are out there picking up what the wind redistributed.
Wednesday, and the driveway has become a full contact sport.
Somebody will be picking leaves out of that back seat for a week.
That door is going to shut whether he is ready or not.
The wind opened it faster than he did and he is still laughing.
Every leaf in the street is queueing to get into that car.
The braids have made the decision and she is going along with it.
That photo is going to look completely different to how it feels.
Thursday, and somebody has decided to enjoy this instead of complaining.
The phone is the only thing out here being held still.
Everyone else on this promenade went home about twenty minutes ago.
The trampoline has relocated and taken the neighbour's wall as a partner.
Somebody is going to be explaining that to somebody else this evening.
Monday, and the garden has rearranged itself without asking anyone.
The palms are fine. The trampoline had opinions about staying put.
It took the wind four seconds to move what took two hours to build.
Every jacaranda on this street is emptying itself onto one man.
That tie has been horizontal since he left the car.
He will be finding purple in that jacket pocket until Friday.
Wednesday morning, and the walk from the parking is now the hard part.
He is bent that far over because standing upright stopped working.
Those eyes are not closed because of the sun.
Friday, and the aloes have not noticed anything unusual at all.
The trees at the fence are taking this worse than he is.
He will sit there until something more interesting happens, which it will not.
That coat is being parted by something other than a brush.
That walk was somebody else's idea and the dog is registering a complaint.
Sunday, and this is about as far as either of them is going.
The lead is doing considerably more work than it was designed for.
He is going to shake all that sand out on the lounge carpet later.
The sea has gone white all the way out and he noticed before anyone.
The jacaranda is redecorating the whole road whether you like it or not.
Saturday, and the wind has strong opinions about your plans for the garden.
That grass on the verge has been lying flat since Thursday.
Somebody is going to sweep all that purple up and somebody is not.
The sky has gone the colour that makes Joburg check the group chat.
The banana leaves are being redesigned in real time and taking it well.
That shade cloth has been drumming since breakfast and nobody can hear the television.
The sea looks calm from up here, which is a complete lie.
Friday, and the humidity has teamed up with the wind against everybody.
Every leaf on that palm is now a slightly different length.
The flag is doing its patriotic duty at about sixty kilometres an hour.
That shade sail is one good gust away from becoming a spinnaker.
The palm has given up on symmetry and committed to one direction.
Nobody on this side of Gqeberha is hanging washing out today.
The aloe is unbothered, which is the entire point of an aloe.
The mountain looks like that about six evenings a year and this is one.
They came out for the sunset and are staying for it despite everything.
Monday, and the wind has completely failed to ruin this.
Nobody's hair is going to survive, and nobody is leaving yet.
Lion's Head is doing the scenery and the wind is doing the comedy.
That jacket has been trying to leave since he got on the bike.
The jacarandas are throwing everything they have at one cyclist.
Tuesday evening, and the ride home has turned into a negotiation.
He is going downhill and still working for every metre of it.
The blossom is coming off those trees faster than he is going under them.
This is the second time this week and they have a system now.
The pegs lost, the wall won, and the neighbours are still laughing.
Nobody is ever going to find that one white sock again.
The wind did the throwing and the neighbour is doing the returning.
One gust, one wall, and two households now know each other much better.
That hair was a decision made indoors about forty minutes ago.
Saturday evening, and the walk from the front door defeated the whole look.
Her hair is going one way, the palm is going the same way, and neither was asked.
Twelve steps from the front door to the car, and the wind took all twelve.
That driveway was swept this morning and has already been refilled.
That tree has been shaped by one wind for about forty years.
The washing goes out at this hour because wind is cheaper than electricity.
The lagoon has gone flat and silver, which fools nobody who lives here.
Everything on this street leans the same way, including the people.
Thursday evening, and the only thing still moving out here is the line.
Bo-Kaap in the last light, and the wind is doing the housekeeping.
That curtain has been outside the window for about an hour now.
The south-easter has found the one open window on the whole street.
Somebody is going to come home to a lounge full of Signal Hill.
The paint is bright, the hill is gold, and the wind is the loudest thing here.
Somebody is going to remember that washing at about two in the morning.
That hedge has been leaning like that since Thursday and it is not straightening.
The security light is picking up things you would rather not watch moving.
Sunday night, and even the washing is refusing to accept it.
Whatever is not pegged down out there is already somebody else's problem.
The sparks are going sideways and the tongs are still going in.
Table Mountain, a braai, and a wind with its own strong opinion.
Saturday, and neither of them will admit the wind is winning.
The tongs are out, so the argument about who cooks is over.
Those coals are doing more for the fence than they are for the meat.
The mountain has its cloth on and the palm is holding the pose.
Wednesday, and the Cape Doctor is doing its rounds a little early.
Nobody walks this road at this hour, and tonight nobody wants to.
That palm has been bent that way so long it thinks it is upright.
The whole street is inside pretending the roof noise is normal.
The aloe is not moving and has no intention of starting now.
That thorn tree has been leaning since before anyone on this street arrived.
The dust is going somewhere and it is not asking permission.
Northern Cape wind does not howl. It leans on things until they give.
Everything out here is either properly rooted or already gone.
The leaves came in. The cat did not go out.
The wind has been delivering leaves to that doormat all evening.
Every leaf on that mat arrived without being invited.
The garden is moving and he has decided the doorway is far enough.
The wind is bringing the outside in and he is letting it come to him.
The banner is holding on better than the palms and it knows it.
Friday night on the promenade and the sea has cleared everyone's diary.
Every palm on this strip is pointing at the same thing tonight.
The city across the water is having a completely different evening.
Nobody is walking that promenade tonight and the lights know it.
